fuente: Condition names: NASA OCHMO-TB-043 Rev A (2023) monitored changes and the NASA Integrated Medical Model (IMM) condition list for 31-180 day missions (nasa.gov/low-earth-orbit-imm-runs). Cards: public first-aid guidance, labeled per card. Provisional until the content team reviews it against IMPACT 1.0.

tarjeta.fuente: NHS, Cuts and grazes (nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes). General first-aid protocol, not NASA's, and not validated for microgravity: steps that rely on gravity (raising the wound above the heart) may not work in flight.
pasos: Wash and dry your hands, or put on gloves from the medical kit, before touching the wound.
Check the wound for debris. If an object is embedded, do not pull it out: press on both sides of it.
If nothing is embedded, press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth or sterile dressing until the bleeding is controlled.
Once the bleeding stops, check the dressing is not too tight: skin beyond it should regain its colour within 2 seconds of being pressed. Re-check every 10 minutes.
Rinse the wound with clean water or sterile wipes, pat it dry and clean the skin around it, wiping away from the wound.
Cover it with a sterile dressing and keep it clean and dry.

Escalate to the flight surgeon now if the cut is deep or large (over about 5 cm), has an embedded object, will not stop bleeding, spurts bright red blood, or there is loss of feeling or movement near it.
que_no_hacer: Do not remove an embedded object.
Do not wrap the dressing so tight that it cuts off circulation.

tarjeta.fuente: NHS, Fainting (nhs.uk/conditions/fainting). General first-aid protocol, not NASA's, and not validated for microgravity: the Earth step of laying the person down and raising their legs relies on gravity.
pasos: Stay calm. Gently shake their shoulders and ask loudly if they are OK.
If they do not respond, call the crew for help, then gently tilt the head back and lift the chin to open the airway.
Check their breathing for at least 10 seconds.
If they are breathing normally, the Earth protocol is to lay them on their back and raise their legs. In flight, keep them restrained in place and tell the flight surgeon.
Most people wake up within about 30 seconds.

Escalate to the flight surgeon at once if they are not breathing, cannot be woken within 1 minute, do not fully recover, have chest pain or an irregular heartbeat, are injured, have a seizure, or fainted while exercising or lying down.
que_no_hacer: Do not treat it as harmless: anyone who faints needs a physician to find the cause.
